selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: This bill requires the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to establish a six-year pilot program for qualifying Medicare beneficiaries with diet-impacted diseases to receive medically tailored home-delivered meals and medical nutrition therapy after hospital discharge, with the goal of improving health outcomes and lowering hospital readmission rates.

affected_groups.effect: Qualifying individuals who meet specific risk, living, and functional limitation criteria may receive medically tailored home-delivered meals and medical nutrition therapy without cost-sharing.
At least 40 eligible hospitals will screen inpatients, coordinate meal preparation and delivery, provide medical nutrition therapy, and submit data to CMS.
Subject to payment reductions by the Secretary to ensure the program remains budget neutral.

key_provisions: Requires CMS to select at least 40 eligible hospitals to participate in a six-year medically tailored home-delivered meals program.

Mandates that participating hospitals provide at least two medically tailored meals per day, meeting at least two-thirds of an individual's daily nutritional needs, for at least 12 weeks following discharge and subsequent rescreenings.
Requires participating hospitals to provide medical nutrition therapy alongside meal delivery for a period ranging from 12 weeks to one year.

Sets eligibility criteria for patients, including having a diet-impacted disease, living at home, not receiving extended or hospice care, having limitations with at least two activities of daily living, and meeting high-risk readmission criteria.
Waives all deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, and other cost-sharing for items and services provided under the program.
Funds the program through the Hospital Insurance Trust Fund while requiring CMS to reduce payments to certain subsection (d) hospitals to maintain budget neutrality.
missing_information: The specific payment amounts and exact formulas that CMS will use to pay participating hospitals.

The exact criteria or additional diseases the Secretary may ultimately determine qualify for the program beyond kidney disease, congestive heart failure, diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
summary_detail.plain_summary: This bill requires the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to establish a six-year pilot program for qualifying Medicare beneficiaries with diet-impacted diseases to receive medically tailored home-delivered meals and medical nutrition therapy after hospital discharge, with the goal of improving health outcomes and lowering hospital readmission rates.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a temporary Medicare payment and service model to test whether providing home-delivered medically tailored meals and nutrition therapy improves clinical health outcomes and reduces hospital readmissions for high-risk patients. The significance score is 70 because it initiates a multi-year federal pilot program involving at least 40 hospitals, changes payment structures under Medicare Part A, and affects hospital funding nationwide to maintain budget neutrality.
